# Next.js App Router — Folder Structure

## Top-level app/ structure

```
app/
├── (app)/          # Authenticated app screens (Route Group — not part of URL)
├── (auth)/         # Authentication screens (login, signup, password reset)
├── (core)/         # Shared components, utilities, and providers
├── api/            # API routes (server-side handlers)
├── error/          # Error pages (unauthorized, etc.)
├── layout.tsx      # Root layout
└── error.tsx       # Global error boundary
```

Route Groups (`(name)/`) organize pages without affecting the URL path.

---

## Per-feature folder pattern (`app/(app)/{feature}/`)

### Collection level (list / new)

```
app/(app)/{feature}/
├── page.tsx                       # list page (collection)
├── {Feature}ListScreen.tsx
├── new/
│   ├── page.tsx                   # creation page
│   └── {Feature}NewScreen.tsx
├── _components/                   # shared by list / new / [id]
└── _hooks/                        # shared by list / new / [id]
```

### Per-record folder (`[id]/`) — VIEW and EDIT split

```
app/(app)/{feature}/[id]/
├── page.tsx                       # router only — redirects to view/ or edit/ based on permission
├── _components/                   # shared by both view and edit
├── _hooks/                        # shared by both view and edit
├── view/
│   ├── page.tsx                   # read-only page
│   ├── {Feature}ViewScreen.tsx
│   ├── _components/
│   └── _hooks/
└── edit/
    ├── page.tsx                   # editable page
    ├── {Feature}EditScreen.tsx
    ├── form.ts                    # Zod schema + Type
    ├── _components/
    └── _hooks/
```

### `[id]/page.tsx` — permission-based redirect

`[id]/` never holds a screen — its `page.tsx` only resolves whether the current user can edit, then redirects to either `view/` or `edit/`.

```tsx
// app/(app)/{feature}/[id]/page.tsx
import { redirect } from "next/navigation"
import { getAuthContext } from "@/app/(core)/_auth/withAuth"
import { canEditResource } from "@/app/api/{feature}/[id]/service"
import { RESOURCE_URL } from "@/app/(core)/endpoints"

type Context = { params: Promise<{ id: string }> }

export default async function Page({ params }: Context) {
  const { id } = await params
  const { userId } = await getAuthContext()
  const canEdit = await canEditResource({ id, userId })
  redirect(canEdit ? RESOURCE_URL.edit(id) : RESOURCE_URL.view(id))
}
```

Why:
- The user can paste `/{feature}/[id]` and always land on the correct page for their role
- Bookmarks, search results, and push notifications survive role changes
- Screen components never branch on "am I view or edit?" — each page is one mode

### Why view and edit are siblings (not nested)

Two routes — `[id]/view` for read-only, `[id]/edit` for editing. Each is a self-contained screen with its own components and hooks. No shared `mode` state, no conditional rendering inside the screen.

This rules out the older pattern of "edit is the default and `view/` is a sub-route under it" — it forced the view screen to live two levels deeper than the edit screen, breaking symmetry.

### Where shared code lives

| Code | Location | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| Common UI (record header, status badge) | `[id]/_components/` | both view and edit |
| Common data hooks (fetch the record) | `[id]/_hooks/` | both view and edit |
| View-only UI (read-only layout) | `[id]/view/_components/` | view only |
| Edit-only UI (form panels) | `[id]/edit/_components/` | edit only |
| Form schema and type | `[id]/edit/form.ts` | edit only |

---

## Shared folder (`app/(core)/`)

Common components, utilities, and providers shared across all screens.

```
app/(core)/
├── _components/        # Shared UI components (ScreenWrapper, PageHeader, etc.)
├── _theme/             # Theme context and configuration
├── _auth/              # Auth helpers and HOCs
├── _hooks/             # Shared hooks across multiple features
├── endpoints.ts        # All URL constants (centralized)
├── logger.ts           # Logger instance
└── errors/             # Error classes and handlers
```

---

## API routes folder (`app/api/`)

Each resource mirrors the URL structure:

```
app/api/{resource}/
├── route.ts        # Next.js API handler (GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE)
├── client.ts       # Client-side fetch functions
├── service.ts      # Business logic
├── db.ts           # DB queries (Drizzle ORM)
└── query.ts        # Query parameter types and validation

app/api/{resource}/[id]/
├── route.ts
├── client.ts
├── service.ts
├── db.ts
└── query.ts
```

---

## Full example — a "resources" feature

```
app/(app)/resources/
├── page.tsx                       # list
├── ResourceListScreen.tsx
├── new/
│   ├── page.tsx
│   └── ResourceNewScreen.tsx
├── _components/
│   └── ResourceCard.tsx
├── _hooks/
│   ├── useResourceList.ts
│   └── useResourceListUrlState.ts
└── [id]/
    ├── page.tsx                   # redirect (view or edit)
    ├── _components/
    │   └── ResourceCommonHeader.tsx
    ├── _hooks/
    │   └── useResource.ts
    ├── view/
    │   ├── page.tsx
    │   ├── ResourceViewScreen.tsx
    │   ├── _components/
    │   │   └── ResourceViewLayout.tsx
    │   └── _hooks/
    │       └── useResourceView.ts
    └── edit/
        ├── page.tsx
        ├── ResourceEditScreen.tsx
        ├── form.ts
        ├── _components/
        │   └── ResourceEditLayout.tsx
        └── _hooks/
            ├── useResourceForm.ts
            ├── useRegisterResource.ts
            ├── useUpdateResource.ts
            └── useDeleteResource.ts
```

---

## Query string handling

When a route accepts query string parameters (e.g. `/resources?filter=active&page=2`),
define the parameter types in `query.ts` under the matching API folder:

```ts
// app/api/resources/query.ts
export type ResourceFilterType = {
  tags?: string[]
  name?: string
  categoryId?: string
}
```

On the frontend, read with `useSearchParams()` and write with a dedicated `useXxxUrlState` hook. See `url-state.md`.

---

## Constraints

- `[id]/page.tsx` is a permission-based redirect only — never a screen
- `[id]/view/` and `[id]/edit/` are siblings under `[id]/` — never nested under one another
- Direct URL `/{feature}/[id]` is supported only via the redirect
- `_components/` and `_hooks/` (plural) folders only — `_hook/` is forbidden in new code
- Screen files use `ViewScreen` / `EditScreen` / `ListScreen` / `NewScreen` suffixes
- Code shared between view and edit lives in `[id]/_components/` and `[id]/_hooks/`
- API URL structure mirrors the frontend structure under `app/api/`
